synthesis.owner_question: Does the LLM query rewrite help or hurt retrieval and answer quality on this corpus at top_k=2 with rerank off?
synthesis.verdict: Rewrite as implemented decisively hurts retrieval (hit@1 0.933->0.856, 9A/1B, p=0.0215, decision-grade) and produces no credible change in answer quality (judged +7.5pt fails cause attribution: 3/15 boundary flips are judge_disagreement on byte-identical answers; deterministic basis coin-consistent 4A/6B p=0.754; strict correct 3=3). The harm is one implementation defect - the wall-clock line injected into every rewrite call (src/llm.py:329, SearchQuery missing from _NO_TIMESTAMP_OUTPUTS at :340) - not the rewrite concept: with echo rows excluded the retrieval effect measures 0.0 points. The one clean positive signal is full-phrasing answers (8 up / 0 down cross-arm, p=0.008, judge basis; deterministic correct-or-partial 19->23), itself distractor-lottery in mechanism.

answer_judge.note: judge_disagreement = 3/15 boundary flips (20%, at judge-limited threshold); deterministic basis 4A/6B p=0.754; strict det correct 3=3

synthesis.judge_limited_note: Cross-session judge noise floor measured at 4 verdict flips on 65 byte-identical answer rows; B-session disagreed with deterministic scorer 23x vs A 11x. Judged-correct deltas under ~5 rows are inside noise on this rubric; use deterministic verdicts for regression detection.
